sanskrit: etaṃ jyotīṃṣi sarvāṇi prakarṣan bhagavān api kurute vitamaskarmā ādityo 'bhipradakṣiṇam
english: Drawing all luminaries along, the blessed Sun, destroyer of darkness, performs his circuit around this mountain.

sanskrit: astaṃ prāpya tataḥ saṃdhyām atikramya divākaraḥ udīcīṃ bhajate kāṣṭhāṃ diśam eṣa vibhāvasuḥ
english: Having reached the western mountain and passed through twilight, the day-maker, this fire-bright one, then courses toward the northern quarter.

sanskrit: sa merum anuvṛttaḥ san punar gacchati pāṇḍava prāṅmukhaḥ savitā devaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ
english: Circumambulating Meru, O Pāṇḍava, the god Sāvitrī turns eastward again, ever devoted to the welfare of all beings.

sanskrit: sa māsaṃ vibhajan kālaṃ bahudhā parvasaṃdhiṣu tathaiva bhagavān somo nakṣatraiḥ saha gacchati
english: Dividing the month and time in many ways at the junctures of fortnights, likewise the blessed Moon travels together with the constellations.

sanskrit: evam eṣa parikramya mahāmerum atandritaḥ bhāvayan sarvabhūtāni punar gacchati mandaram
english: Thus having circumambulated great Meru without fatigue, nourishing all beings, he returns again to Mount Mandara.

sanskrit: tathā tamisrahā devo mayūkhair bhāvayañ jagat mārgam etad asaṃbādham ādityaḥ parivartate
english: Thus the god who destroys darkness, nourishing the world with his rays, the Āditya revolves along this unobstructed path.

sanskrit: sisṛkṣuḥ śiśirāṇy eṣa dakṣiṇāṃ bhajate diśam tataḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni kālaḥ śiśiram ṛcchati
english: Desiring to create cold, he moves toward the southern quarter; thereupon all beings reach the cold season in due time.

sanskrit: sthāvarāṇāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ jaṅgamānāṃ ca tejasā tejāṃsi samupādatte nivṛttaḥ san vibhāvasuḥ
english: Turning back, the fire-bright one draws up with his radiance the vital energies of both stationary and moving beings.

sanskrit: tataḥ svedaḥ klamas tandrī glāniś ca bhajate narān prāṇibhiḥ satataṃ svapno hy abhīkṣṇaṃ ca niṣevyate
english: Then sweat, weariness, drowsiness, and languor overtake men, and creatures are constantly and repeatedly given to sleep.

sanskrit: evam etad anirdeśyaṃ mārgam āvṛtya bhānumān punaḥ sṛjati varṣāṇi bhagavān bhāvayan prajāḥ
english: Thus the blessed, radiant one, having traversed this indescribable path, again sends forth rains, nourishing all creatures.

sanskrit: vṛṣṭimārutasaṃtāpaiḥ sukhaiḥ sthāvarajaṅgamān vardhayan sumahātejāḥ punaḥ pratinivartate
english: The one of very great brilliance, nurturing stationary and moving beings with rain, wind, heat, and pleasant seasons, turns back once more.

sanskrit: evam eṣa caran pārtha kālacakram atandritaḥ prakarṣan sarvabhūtāni savitā parivartate
english: Thus Sāvitrī, O Pārtha, moving tirelessly and drawing all beings along, revolves the wheel of time.

sanskrit: saṃtatā gatir etasya naiṣa tiṣṭhati pāṇḍava ādāyaiva tu bhūtānāṃ tejo visṛjate punaḥ
english: His motion is unceasing; he never stands still, O Pāṇḍava — having drawn up the vitality of beings, he releases it again.

sanskrit: vibhajan sarvabhūtānām āyuḥ karma ca bhārata ahorātrān kalāḥ kāṣṭhāḥ sṛjaty eṣa sadā vibhuḥ
english: Allotting to all beings their lifespan and the fruits of their deeds, O Bhārata, the all-pervading one ever creates days, nights, moments, and instants.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmin nagendre vasatāṃ tu teṣāṃ; mahātmanāṃ sadvratam āsthitānām ratiḥ pramodaś ca babhūva teṣām; ākāṅkṣatāṃ darśanam arjunasya
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While those great-souled ones dwelling on that king of mountains observed their sacred vows, delight and joy arose among them — yet all the while they longed for the sight of Arjuna.

sanskrit: tān vīryayuktān suviśuddhasattvāṃs; tejasvinaḥ satyadhṛtipradhānān saṃprīyamāṇā bahavo 'bhijagmur; gandharvasaṃghāś ca maharṣayaś ca
english: Gladdened by them — those men of prowess, utterly pure in nature, radiant, foremost in truth and steadfastness — many companies of gandharvas and great sages came to visit.

sanskrit: taṃ pādapaiḥ puṣpadharair upetaṃ; nagottamaṃ prāpya mahārathānām manaḥprasādaḥ paramo babhūva; yathā divaṃ prāpya marudgaṇānām
english: Reaching that finest of mountains adorned with flower-bearing trees, the great warriors experienced supreme serenity of mind, even as the Maruts feel upon reaching heaven.

sanskrit: mayūrahaṃsasvananāditāni; puṣpopakīrṇāni mahācalasya śṛṅgāṇi sānūni ca paśyamānā; gireḥ paraṃ harṣam avāpya tasthuḥ
english: Beholding the peaks and plateaus of that great mountain, resonant with the cries of peacocks and swans and strewn with blossoms, they stood there, seized with supreme joy at the sight.

sanskrit: sākṣāt kubereṇa kṛtāś ca tasmin; nagottame saṃvṛtakūlarodhasaḥ kādambakāraṇḍavahaṃsajuṣṭāḥ; padmākulāḥ puṣkariṇīr apaśyan
english: On that finest of mountains they beheld lotus-thronged pools made by Kubera himself, with banks fully enclosed, frequented by kadamba ducks, sheldrakes, and swans.

sanskrit: krīḍāpradeśāṃś ca samṛddharūpān; sucitramālyāvṛtajātaśobhān maṇipravekān sumanoharāṃś ca; yathā bhaveyur dhanadasya rājñaḥ
english: And they saw pleasure-groves of surpassing beauty, resplendent with varied garlands, richly endowed with gems, altogether charming — such as would befit the king of treasures himself.

sanskrit: anekavarṇaiś ca sugandhibhiś ca; mahādrumaiḥ saṃtatam abhramālibhiḥ tapaḥpradhānāḥ satataṃ carantaḥ; śṛṅgaṃ gireś cintayituṃ na śekuḥ
english: Those dedicated to austerity, constantly roaming among the great trees of many hues and sweet fragrances, garlanded perpetually with clouds, could not fathom the full extent of that mountain's peak.

sanskrit: svatejasā tasya nagottamasya; mahauṣadhīnāṃ ca tathā prabhāvāt vibhaktabhāvo na babhūva kaś cid; aharniśānāṃ puruṣapravīra
english: By the inherent radiance of that finest of mountains and by the power of its great herbs, O best of men, no distinction whatsoever was perceptible between day and night.

sanskrit: yam āsthitaḥ sthāvarajaṅgamāni; vibhāvasur bhāvayate 'mitaojāḥ tasyodayaṃ cāstamayaṃ ca vīrās; tatra sthitās te dadṛśur nṛsiṃhāḥ
english: The rising and setting of that one — the fire-bright, immeasurably powerful Sun by whom stationary and moving beings are nourished — those lion-like heroes saw while stationed there.

sanskrit: raves tamisrāgamanirgamāṃs te; tathodayaṃ cāstamayaṃ ca vīrāḥ samāvṛtāḥ prekṣya tamonudasya; gabhastijālaiḥ pradiśo diśaś ca
english: Those heroes, enveloped and enfolded by the sun's net of rays, watched the arrivals and departures of darkness with the sun's rising and setting, along with the directions and intermediate quarters.

sanskrit: svādhyāyavantaḥ satatakriyāś ca; dharmapradhānāś ca śucivratāś ca satye sthitās tasya mahārathasya; satyavratasyāgamanapratīkṣāḥ
english: Devoted to scriptural recitation, constant in their rites, foremost in righteousness, pure in their vows, established in truth — they awaited the return of that great warrior who had sworn to truth.

sanskrit: ihaiva harṣo 'stu samāgatānāṃ; kṣipraṃ kṛtāstreṇa dhanaṃjayena iti bruvantaḥ paramāśiṣas te; pārthās tapoyogaparā babhūvuḥ
english: Uttering the highest blessings — "May joy come quickly to all of us assembled here through Dhanañjaya who has mastered the weapons" — those sons of Pṛthā became absorbed in the discipline of austerity.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā vicitrāṇi girau vanāni; kirīṭinaṃ cintayatām abhīkṣṇam babhūva rātrir divasaś ca teṣāṃ; saṃvatsareṇaiva samānarūpaḥ
english: Though beholding the wondrous forests on that mountain, constantly thinking of the diademed one, each night and day passed for them as if it were a full year.

sanskrit: yadaiva dhaumyānumate mahātmā; kṛtvā jaṭāḥ pravrajitaḥ sa jiṣṇuḥ tadaiva teṣāṃ na babhūva harṣaḥ; kuto ratis tadgatamānasānām
english: From the very moment the great-souled Jiṣṇu, with Dhaumya's approval, bound his hair in matted locks and set forth, joy left them — how could there be any pleasure for those whose minds had gone with him?

sanskrit: bhrātur niyogāt tu yudhiṣṭhirasya; vanād asau vāraṇamattagāmī yat kāmyakāt pravrajitaḥ sa jiṣṇus; tadaiva te śokahatā babhūvuḥ
english: By the command of his brother Yudhiṣṭhira, from that forest, that Jiṣṇu who walks like a rutting elephant had set forth from Kāmyaka — from that very moment they were struck with grief.

sanskrit: tathā tu taṃ cintayatāṃ sitāśvam; astrārthinaṃ vāsavam abhyupetam māso 'tha kṛcchreṇa tadā vyatītas; tasmin nage bhārata bhāratānām
english: Thus thinking of him — the white-horsed one, the seeker of weapons who had gone to Indra — a month passed with difficulty for the Bhāratas on that mountain, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid dharisaṃprayuktaṃ; mahendravāhaṃ sahasopayātam vidyutprabhaṃ prekṣya mahārathānāṃ; harṣo 'rjunaṃ cintayatāṃ babhūva
english: Then one day, when those great warriors thinking of Arjuna suddenly beheld the great chariot of Indra drawn by bay horses approaching with lightning's brilliance, joy arose in them.

sanskrit: sa dīpyamānaḥ sahasāntarikṣaṃ; prakāśayan mātalisaṃgṛhītaḥ babhau maholkeva ghanāntarasthā; śikheva cāgner jvalitā vidhūmā
english: Blazing and suddenly illuminating the sky, guided by Matali, it shone like a great meteor in the midst of clouds, or like a smokeless tongue of fire blazing upward.

sanskrit: tam āsthitaḥ saṃdadṛśe kirīṭī; sragvī varāṇy ābharaṇāni bibhrat dhanaṃjayo vajradharaprabhāvaḥ; śriyā jvalan parvatam ājagāma
english: Mounted on it, the diademed one was seen — Dhanañjaya, garlanded and wearing ornaments of finest quality, blazing with the splendor of the thunderbolt-bearer, came to the mountain aflame with glory.

sanskrit: sa śailam āsādya kirīṭamālī; mahendravāhād avaruhya tasmāt dhaumyasya pādāv abhivādya pūrvam; ajātaśatros tadanantaraṃ ca
english: Having reached the mountain, the crown-garlanded one descended from that chariot of mighty Indra and, bowing first at the feet of Dhaumya, then next at those of Ajātaśatru.

sanskrit: vṛkodarasyāpi vavanda pādau; mādrīsutābhyām abhivāditaś ca sametya kṛṣṇāṃ parisāntvya caināṃ; prahvo 'bhavad bhrātur upahvare saḥ
english: He bowed also at the feet of Vṛkodara, was greeted in turn by the sons of Mādrī, and having met Kṛṣṇa and comforted her, he stood humbly at his brother's side.

sanskrit: babhūva teṣāṃ paramaḥ praharṣas; tenāprameyeṇa samāgatānām sa cāpi tān prekṣya kirīṭamālī; nananda rājānam abhipraśaṃsan
english: There arose in all of them the greatest joy upon being reunited with that immeasurable hero; and he too, the crown-garlanded one, seeing them, rejoiced and offered praise to the king.

sanskrit: yam āsthitaḥ sapta jaghāna pūgān; diteḥ sutānāṃ namucer nihantā tam indravāhaṃ samupetya pārthāḥ; pradakṣiṇaṃ cakrur adīnasattvāḥ
english: Approaching that chariot of Indra — the slayer of Namuci, by riding which he had slain seven hosts of Diti's sons — the Pārthas of undaunted spirit circumambulated it reverently.

sanskrit: te mātaleś cakrur atīva hṛṣṭāḥ; satkāram agryaṃ surarājatulyam sarvaṃ yathāvac ca divaukasas tān; papracchur enaṃ kururājaputrāḥ
english: They, exceedingly delighted, rendered Matali the highest honor befitting the king of the gods; and the sons of the Kuru king duly asked him all things concerning the dwellers in heaven.

sanskrit: tān apy asau mātalir abhyanandat; piteva putrān anuśiṣya cainān yayau rathenāpratimaprabheṇa; punaḥ sakāśaṃ tridiveśvarasya
english: Matali greeted them in return and, having instructed them as a father would his sons, departed in that chariot of incomparable brilliance back to the presence of the lord of the triple heaven.

sanskrit: gate tu tasmin varadevavāhe; śakrātmajaḥ sarvaripupramāthī śakreṇa dattāni dadau mahātmā; mahādhanāny uttamarūpavanti divākarābhāṇi vibhūṣaṇāni; prītaḥ priyāyai sutasomamātre
english: When that divine chariot had departed, the great-souled son of Śakra, destroyer of all enemies, joyfully gave to his beloved — the mother of his son Soma — the great and most beautiful ornaments radiant as the sun that Śakra had given him.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa teṣāṃ kurupuṃgavānāṃ; teṣāṃ ca sūryāgnisamaprabhāṇām viprarṣabhāṇām upaviśya madhye; sarvaṃ yathāvat kathayāṃ babhūva
english: Then, sitting in the midst of those foremost Kurus, those brilliant as the sun and fire, and those best of brahmins, he recounted everything exactly as it had occurred.

sanskrit: evaṃ mayāstrāṇy upaśikṣitāni; śakrāc ca vātāc ca śivāc ca sākṣāt tathaiva śīlena samādhinā ca; prītāḥ surā me sahitāḥ sahendrāḥ
english: "Thus were the weapons mastered by me — from Śakra, from Vata, and from Śiva in person; and likewise through good conduct and deep concentration the gods, together with Indra, were pleased with me."

sanskrit: saṃkṣepato vai sa viśuddhakarmā; tebhyaḥ samākhyāya divi praveśam mādrīsutābhyāṃ sahitaḥ kirīṭī; suṣvāpa tām āvasatiṃ pratītaḥ
english: Having narrated in brief his entry into heaven to them, the diademed one of pure deeds, together with the sons of Mādrī, lay down contentedly to sleep in that dwelling.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etasminn eva kāle tu sarvavāditranisvanaḥ babhūva tumulaḥ śabdas tv antarikṣe divaukasām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: At that very time a tumultuous sound of all musical instruments arose in the sky — the sound of the celestial dwellers.

sanskrit: rathanemisvanaś caiva ghaṇṭāśabdaś ca bhārata pṛthag vyālamṛgāṇāṃ ca pakṣiṇāṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ
english: The sound of chariot wheels, the ringing of bells, O Bhārata, along with separately the cries of great serpent-beasts and birds of every kind.

sanskrit: taṃ samantād anuyayur gandharvāpsarasas tathā vimānaiḥ sūryasaṃkāśair devarājam ariṃdamam
english: Gandharvas and apsarases followed on all sides the enemy-subduing king of the gods in aerial cars radiant as the sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa haribhir yuktaṃ jāmbūnadapariṣkṛtam meghanādinam āruhya śriyā paramayā jvalan
english: Then he, blazing with supreme splendor, mounted the thundering chariot harnessed with bay horses, adorned with gold of the Jambū river.

sanskrit: pārthān abhyājagāmāśu devarājaḥ puraṃdaraḥ āgatya ca sahasrākṣo rathād avaruroha vai
english: The king of gods, Purandara, swiftly came to the Pārthas; and having arrived, the thousand-eyed one descended from his chariot.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvaiva mahātmānaṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ śrīmān devarājam upāgamat
english: At the very sight of that great-souled one, the glorious Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira, together with his brothers, approached the king of the gods.

sanskrit: pūjayām āsa caivātha vidhivad bhūridakṣiṇaḥ yathārham amitātmānaṃ vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: The munificent one then worshipped him duly according to prescribed rites, honoring the one of boundless spirit with the acts enjoined by sacred rule.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayaś ca tejasvī praṇipatya puraṃdaram bhṛtyavat praṇatas tasthau devarājasamīpataḥ
english: And the radiant Dhanañjaya, having prostrated himself before Purandara, stood bowed like a servant near the king of the gods.

sanskrit: āpyāyata mahātejāḥ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dhanaṃjayam abhiprekṣya vinītaṃ sthitam antike
english: The greatly radiant son of Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira, was filled with joy seeing Dhanañjaya standing humbly nearby.

sanskrit: jaṭilaṃ devarājasya tapoyuktam akalmaṣam harṣeṇa mahatāviṣṭaḥ phalgunasyātha darśanāt
english: Seized with great joy at the sight of Phalguna — his hair matted, devoted to austerity, free of all taint, standing before the king of gods.

sanskrit: taṃ tathādīnamanasaṃ rājānaṃ harṣasaṃplutam uvāca vacanaṃ dhīmān devarājaḥ puraṃdaraḥ
english: To that king whose mind was thus free of dejection and flooded with joy, the wise king of the gods, Purandara, spoke these words.

sanskrit: tvam imāṃ pṛthivīṃ rājan praśāsiṣyasi pāṇḍava svasti prāpnuhi kaunteya kāmyakaṃ punar āśramam
english: "You shall rule this earth, O king, O Pāṇḍava. Fare well, O son of Kuntī; return again to the Kāmyaka hermitage."

sanskrit: astrāṇi labdhāni ca pāṇḍavena; sarvāṇi mattaḥ prayatena rājan kṛtapriyaś cāsmi dhanaṃjayena; jetuṃ na śakyas tribhir eṣa lokaiḥ
english: "All weapons have been obtained by the Pāṇḍava from me with concentrated effort, O king; Dhanañjaya has done me a great service — this one cannot be conquered by the three worlds."

sanskrit: evam uktvā sahasrākṣaḥ kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram jagāma tridivaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the thousand-eyed one, pleased and extolled by the great sages, departed for the triple heaven, leaving Kuntī's son Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: dhaneśvaragṛhasthānāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ samāgamam śakreṇa ya imaṃ vidvān adhīyīta samāhitaḥ
english: Whoever, knowing this, recites with concentrated mind the reunion of the Pāṇḍavas dwelling in the house of the lord of wealth, together with Śakra —

sanskrit: saṃvatsaraṃ brahmacārī niyataḥ saṃśitavrataḥ sa jīveta nirābādhaḥ susukhī śaradāṃ śatam
english: — observing celibacy for a year, self-restrained, with sharpened vows, shall live free from affliction and in great happiness for a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yathāgataṃ gate śakre bhrātṛbhiḥ saha saṃgataḥ kṛṣṇayā caiva bībhatsur dharmaputram apūjayat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Śakra had departed as he came, Bībhatsu, reunited with his brothers and with Kṛṣṇa, paid homage to the son of Dharma.

sanskrit: abhivādayamānaṃ tu mūrdhny upāghrāya pāṇḍavam harṣagadgadayā vācā prahṛṣṭo 'rjunam abravīt
english: Smelling the head of the Pāṇḍava as he made his obeisance, the king spoke to Arjuna in a voice thick with joy, himself overjoyed.

sanskrit: katham arjuna kālo 'yaṃ svarge vyatigatas tava kathaṃ cāstrāṇy avāptāni devarājaś ca toṣitaḥ
english: "How, Arjuna, did you spend this time in heaven? How were the weapons obtained? And how was the king of the gods pleased?"

sanskrit: samyag vā te gṛhītāni kaccid astrāṇi bhārata kaccit surādhipaḥ prīto rudraś cāstrāṇy adāt tava
english: "Were the weapons properly mastered by you, O Bhārata? Was the lord of the gods satisfied? And did Rudra give you weapons?"

sanskrit: yathā dṛṣṭaś ca te śakro bhagavān vā pinākadhṛk yathā cāstrāṇy avāptāni yathā cārādhitaś ca te
english: "How did you see Śakra, or the blessed bearer of the Pināka bow? How were the weapons obtained? And how was he propitiated by you?"

sanskrit: yathoktavāṃs tvāṃ bhagavāñ śatakratur ariṃdama kṛtapriyas tvayāsmīti tac ca te kiṃ priyaṃ kṛtam etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ vistareṇa mahādyute
english: "How did the blessed Śatakratu say to you, O subduer of enemies, 'You have done me a service' — and what service did you render him? I wish to hear all this in full detail, O greatly resplendent one."

sanskrit: yathā tuṣṭo mahādevo devarājaś ca te 'nagha yac cāpi vajrapāṇes te priyaṃ kṛtam ariṃdama etad ākhyāhi me sarvam akhilena dhanaṃjaya
english: "How was Mahādeva pleased with you, and the king of gods, O sinless one? And what service did you render to the thunderbolt-bearer, O subduer of foes? Tell me all of this fully and completely, O Dhanañjaya."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca śṛṇu hanta mahārāja vidhinā yena dṛṣṭavān śatakratum ahaṃ devaṃ bhagavantaṃ ca śaṃkaram
english: Arjuna said: Listen, O great king — hear the manner in which I saw Śatakratu and the blessed god Shankara.

sanskrit: vidyām adhītya tāṃ rājaṃs tvayoktām arimardana bhavatā ca samādiṣṭas tapase prasthito vanam
english: Having studied that lore you spoke of, O king, O crusher of enemies, and being directed by you to austerity, I set out into the forest.

sanskrit: bhṛgutuṅgam atho gatvā kāmyakād āsthitas tapaḥ ekarātroṣitaḥ kaṃ cid apaśyaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ pathi
english: Going from Kāmyaka to Bhṛgutuṅga, I undertook austerity; and having stayed one night, I saw on the path a certain brahmin.

sanskrit: sa mām apṛcchat kaunteya kvāsi gantā bravīhi me tasmā avitathaṃ sarvam abruvaṃ kurunandana
english: He asked me, 'O son of Kuntī, where are you going? Tell me.' To him I spoke all things without untruth, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: sa tathyaṃ mama tac chrutvā brāhmaṇo rājasattama apūjayata māṃ rājan prītimāṃś cābhavan mayi
english: That brahmin, having heard this truth from me, O best of kings, honored me, O king, and was pleased with me.

sanskrit: tato mām abravīt prītas tapa ātiṣṭha bhārata tapasvī nacireṇa tvaṃ drakṣyase vibudhādhipam
english: Then he said to me, pleased: 'Undertake austerity, O Bhārata, O ascetic; before long you shall behold the lord of the wise gods.'

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ vacanāt tasya girim āruhya śaiśiram tapo 'tapyaṃ mahārāja māsaṃ mūlaphalāśanaḥ
english: Then, by his word, I climbed the Shaishira mountain and practiced austerity, O great king, for a month, living on roots and fruits.

sanskrit: dvitīyaś cāpi me māso jalaṃ bhakṣayato gataḥ nirāhāras tṛtīye 'tha māse pāṇḍavanandana
english: A second month also passed for me subsisting on water alone; then in the third month, O joy of the Pāṇḍavas, I took no food at all.

sanskrit: ūrdhvabāhuś caturthaṃ tu māsam asmi sthitas tadā na ca me hīyate prāṇas tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: For the fourth month I stood with arms raised aloft; and yet my vital breath did not diminish — that seemed like a wonder.

sanskrit: caturthe samabhikrānte prathame divase gate varāhasaṃsthitaṃ bhūtaṃ matsamīpam upāgamat
english: When the fourth month had fully passed and the first day was gone, a creature in the form of a boar approached near me.

sanskrit: nighnan prothena pṛthivīṃ vilikhaṃś caraṇair api saṃmārjañ jaṭhareṇorvīṃ vivartaṃś ca muhur muhuḥ
english: It was striking the earth with its snout, scratching with its hooves as well, sweeping the ground with its belly, and turning about again and again.

sanskrit: anu tasyāparaṃ bhūtaṃ mahat kairātasaṃsthitam dhanurbāṇāsimat prāptaṃ strīgaṇānugataṃ tadā
english: Behind it came another great creature in the form of a Kirata hunter, arrived bearing bow, arrows, and sword, followed by a host of women.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ dhanur ādāya tathākṣayyau maheṣudhī atāḍayaṃ śareṇātha tad bhūtaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
english: Then I took up my bow and the two inexhaustible quivers and struck that hair-raising creature with an arrow.

sanskrit: yugapat tat kirātaś ca vikṛṣya balavad dhanuḥ abhyājaghne dṛḍhataraṃ kampayann iva me manaḥ
english: Simultaneously that Kirata, drawing his bow with great force, struck back even more powerfully, making my mind tremble.
